title: Getting started
summary: This is your control room for the CA Autobody website. You manage published content here without touching website code.
steps: Sign in with your authorized work email and verification code.
On the redesigned Dashboard, review the content metrics, drafts, and quick module shortcuts. Navigate with the floating sidebar.
Collapse or expand the floating sidebar on desktop. Its scrollbar is invisible but you can still scroll navigation by wheel, touch or keyboard. Open the menu on mobile.
Check the status pill on each item. Draft is private; Published is live; Deleted means archived from public view.
Use the profile at the bottom of the menu to sign out after your session.

title: Create, preview, publish
summary: Use the same safe editorial workflow for services, blogs, FAQs, offers, areas and gallery content.
website: All content modules in the left sidebar
steps: Open the relevant module and select New, or choose Edit on an existing record.
Start with a clear title, then complete content fields and upload approved images.
The Publish panel and all editor settings panels remain in the normal page flow. Scroll the page to reach them; they do not stick to the viewport.
Use Save draft while the item is still being prepared. Do not publish incomplete pages.
Open Preview on the saved record to see the page rendered with the website's layout. The preview is visible only to authorized CMS staff.
Review on desktop and mobile. Check headings, text, images, links and any publication or placement settings.
Select Publish or Update only when the page has been approved. An Editor account may need a Publisher or Admin to publish.
Reopen the published page through Preview or the View website link to confirm the live result.
caution: Preview reflects the last saved version. Unsaved local edits must be saved before they appear in a private preview; don't save a live Published record as Draft without considering its public visibility.

title: Find and manage records
summary: Each content library includes search, visible status counts, and actions for individual entries.
website: Services, Blogs, Offers, Areas, Gallery and FAQ module lists
steps: Choose All, Published, Draft or Deleted above the listing to narrow the records.
Use Search or a category filter to locate the record you need.
Open Edit to modify content or Preview to inspect the last saved version privately.
Choose Duplicate to create an independent Draft copy before testing a large revision.
Use Delete only when you intend to remove the item from the public website. Confirm the dialog. This is a soft delete: the CMS retains its record for auditing.
Select Refresh CMS if changes made by someone else aren't yet reflected on your screen.

title: Services and brand pages
summary: Manage Service and Brand content in the main editor, with separate compact Hero Background and Right-Side Image cards below Page Settings.
website: Website: /services and /services/[slug]; homepage Services menu / service slider, when enabled
steps: Open Services and select New or Edit. Enter the service title and edit the introduction and content in the main editor column.
In the right settings column, use Publish to save a draft, preview the last saved version, or publish when authorized. The column scrolls normally rather than staying fixed.
Under Page Settings, verify the URL slug, SEO title and existing website-placement toggles.
In Hero Background, click Upload image or Replace image. Choose a wide photograph; the system prepares a WebP version and shows a landscape preview.
For Editorial and Brand layouts, use the separate Right-Side Image card to upload a portrait or landscape photograph. The two image fields are independent.
Use Remove to clear an image. For an existing link, expand Use image URL instead. Wait for the WebP ready confirmation when uploading a file.
Choose the Page layout on the main canvas and edit the supporting sections. Save draft, then use Preview to inspect the saved record.
Publish or Update after approval. After publishing, the website uses the independent right-side image. The original website image is used if this field has not been set.
For order and visibility within the global Services menu and homepage slider, open the separate Menu arrangement module; per-Service Page Settings still determines eligibility.

title: Mega Menu and Homepage Slider ordering
summary: Arrange published Service links in the global Services Mega Menu and homepage Services Slider independently, without altering the website design.
website: Admin: /caautobodyadmin/menu-arrangement; published output: global Services dropdown and homepage service slider
steps: Open Content → Menu arrangement from the floating sidebar.
Choose Services Mega Menu or Homepage Services Slider. Each tab keeps a different order and set of visible entries.
Drag a service using its grip handle to a new position; for keyboard or touchscreen, use its Position selector (Alt + arrow keys also work on the focused drag handle).
Select Hide to remove a link from that website location without unpublishing the actual Service. Use + Add on an available published service to include it again.
If a Service isn't available, edit that Service's Page Settings and enable the corresponding menu or homepage slider placement, then publish it.

Click Save arrangement, then open the website. Under normal connectivity open tabs should refresh after a publication-version change; page refresh on a different device can be delayed by the connectivity/polling fallback.
If you receive a conflict warning, another administrator changed the order. Reload, compare, and then reapply your intended order.
caution: Only Publisher or Admin roles may save ordering. The menu/slider appearance is unchanged; this module changes only which services appear and their order. No draft service is eligible.

title: Blog articles
summary: Articles use a separate editor for metadata and a draggable body builder.
steps: Choose Blogs → New article. Enter title, category, display date, slug, excerpt and featured image.
Save the article first to open its full article builder.
In the builder, add Heading, Text, List, Image or Callout blocks.
Drag blocks by their grip handles to change reading order. Keyboard drag support is available via the block controls.
Save the changed blocks. The Unsaved changes notice shows when there is work you have not saved.
Select Preview to inspect the saved article on the real website template; then Publish or Update.

title: Frequently asked questions
summary: Answers are grouped by category. Visibility is separate from the publishing state.
steps: Choose FAQ → Add FAQ or Edit an existing question.
Enter the question, answer and appropriate category.
Use Visible on the public FAQ page to show or hide the answer where that setting is supported.
Save the draft and use Preview to review the content privately.
Publish to make an approved, visible FAQ appear on the public FAQ page.
Use Duplicate to prepare an alternate answer without overwriting the original.

title: Offers
summary: Manage the headlines, images and detail paragraphs of public offers.
steps: Choose Offers → New offer.
Enter title, slug, SEO title, image, introduction and body paragraphs.
Add key points, using one point per line.
Save draft; choose Preview to see the offer page.
Publish or Update when it is ready. Use Delete to remove an obsolete offer from public view.

title: Areas we serve
summary: Manage the primary suburb pages. The full suburb map-pins dataset is separate from those editable pages.
steps: Choose Areas we serve → New area.
Enter the suburb name, slug, SEO title, introduction and page image.
Fill in the map description and exact latitude/longitude for that dedicated area when applicable.
Save draft and Preview before publishing.
Do not assume that editing these ten dedicated pages changes the separate extended-suburbs pin dataset.

title: Gallery and images
summary: Organize approved repair imagery in a draggable bento grid, with one combined preview for the complete gallery.
steps: Open Gallery. Images are arranged in the same responsive bento pattern used for the website gallery.
Select Add image. Choose or drag in a supported photo; the CMS compresses it before transfer and the server validates/converts it to WebP.
Wait for the WebP ready message and check the original and optimized file sizes. Add caption and category; save the record as Draft, then Publish if approved.
Select Preview gallery at the top to see the whole published gallery; Include drafts is a private editor-only preview.
Clear Search and choose All. Publisher/Admin accounts can drag an image by its grip to a different bento position. Keyboard users can focus the grip and use arrow keys.
Select Save layout to persist the image order. Other open admin tabs reload the saved order automatically; the public gallery uses the existing publication refresh mechanism.
Open the live gallery page to verify the published order and appearance. Repositioning changes the order, not the aspect ratio, public layout code or caption.
caution: Gallery changes do not save until Save layout succeeds. Do not leave the page with an unsaved order. A different administrator may have edited the gallery; refresh and reconcile if a conflict is reported.

title: Smart image uploading and placement
summary: Upload a large photo once; the CMS optimizes it to WebP while preserving its proportions and the existing public website design.
website: CMS-only image fields in Services, Blogs, Offers, Areas, Gallery and relevant brand/service content sections
steps: Open an image field in the editor and click Choose or drop photo, or drag a supported JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or browser-supported HEIC image into the upload area.
The browser first reduces the pixel dimensions and file size if necessary. It then uploads the compressed WebP to the authenticated CMS server; a progress indicator shows transfer status.
The server validates and converts the image to WebP and stores it privately in Supabase staging until the surrounding content is published.
Check the WebP ready confirmation: it displays actual original and optimized sizes, plus the output dimensions. Always inspect the image preview.
Hero image fields use a wide-image optimization profile without cutting pixels off. On the public website the existing hero frame determines how a picture is cropped.
Supporting article, portrait, featured, and Gallery pictures preserve their proportions. The Gallery bento pattern is unchanged.
Save Draft, open the private content Preview, adjust the image if needed, then Publish when the layout is approved.
caution: Large images are supported within safe processing limits (32 MB original file, 100 megapixels). The CMS cannot guarantee a particular KB result, and HEIC depends on browser/server decoder support. Uploads are not automatically published.

title: Live updates and synchronization
summary: CMS lists and counters stay current without unnecessary manual refreshes, using automatic notifications and a safe polling fallback.
website: Admin dashboard, Services, Blogs, Gallery, FAQ, Offers, Areas, Contacts, Audit and the existing published-page refresh system
steps: Save, publish, duplicate or delete an item. Wait for a successful server response before leaving the editor.
The CMS signals other open tabs on the same browser immediately. Matching lists refetch using existing authenticated API endpoints.
Publishing events from other sessions use the existing public-content version signal where configured. Other edits appear through periodic synchronization while tabs are visible.
Dashboard totals refresh automatically, and Contacts and Audit Log periodically check for new records.
Changes arriving remotely never replace unsaved text typed into an open editor. Finish or discard local edits and reopen the record if another administrator changed it.

Published routes are revalidated by existing server-side publishing logic. The public site retains its exact design and uses its existing publication listener; its behavior is subject to installed database trigger and infrastructure support.
If a connection drops, reconnect and allow the automatic refresh to recover; manual Refresh is still available as a fallback.
caution: Changes across different users are near-real-time, not guaranteed instant. Never use a success notice as proof until the server confirms the write; review a published page for important updates.

title: Contact management
summary: Handle customer enquiries and the team's follow-up workflow.
website: Website: contact forms at /contact and other website entry points
steps: Open Contact management from Operations.
Review the customer's submitted details and the requested service.
Update the enquiry status as the team responds and resolves it.
Use the stored details only for its intended enquiry workflow; do not share personal contact details outside authorized staff.

title: Analytics and export
summary: The Google Site Kit-inspired design displays the existing GA4 and Google Search Console reporting—not synthetic traffic.
website: Admin only: /caautobodyadmin/analytics (nothing is published on the website)
steps: Open Analytics in the sidebar.
Choose Last 28 days, Day, Month, Year or Custom range; fill the relevant dates.
Select Apply period to fetch that period's verified GA4/Search Console report.
Read real GA4 and Search Console values from the compact Site Kit-inspired sections: charts, devices, top pages, search queries, and engagement.
Select Export CSV for spreadsheet analysis or Export PDF for a downloadable book-style report of the currently displayed period.
If connection is unavailable, follow the setup message. Export buttons remain disabled until a real report is loaded.

title: Team, authentication and audit
summary: Permissions and audit history stay in place, even though the interface looks different.
steps: Go to Team & access to review authorized accounts and roles.
Use work emails, restrict publisher access, and never share verification codes.
Editors can work on drafts; only the permitted roles can publish.
Use Audit log to investigate who changed an item and when.
Delete is an archived status, not a database wipe. Confirm important changes before deleting.

title: Settings and website placement
summary: Business details feed into the public website, while integrations remain in deployment configuration.
website: Website: business phone, address, contact details and related locations
steps: Open Settings in the sidebar.
Update the correct business name, email, phone and address.
Save verified details only; some values are displayed across multiple public pages.
Reopen the affected public page to confirm the changes.
GA4 tracking and private Search Console credentials are managed in deployment environment variables, not via the CMS form.

title: Checks before asking for help
summary: Most editor problems can be narrowed down without touching code or Supabase.
steps: If Preview does not show new text, save the item first and reopen the private preview.
If Publish is unavailable, check your CMS role.
If an image does not appear, check upload confirmation, the accepted file type and the URL preview.
If a large photo fails, check that it is no larger than the 32 MB safety limit and that the browser supports decoding it; try JPG or PNG if HEIC is unsupported.
If updates appear stale, ensure the tab is online and visible. Authorized lists poll periodically when idle; recent saves also signal other tabs.
If you cannot reorder the Gallery, verify you have a Publisher/Admin role, switch to All, and clear Search before dragging. Use arrow keys on the grip for keyboard sorting.
If Analytics shows a connection error, check the reporting configuration with an administrator; do not enter private keys in content fields.
If a save fails, read the error toast and avoid resubmitting until you know whether the record changed.

If a newly uploaded Service/Brand right-side image appears in the editor but not on the public page, this release preserves existing public hardcoded image bindings. Request approval for the small public-data-binding update; do not alter the hero background to compensate.

If a published edit is missing on the live site, verify the record is Published, check its image/placement settings, and have an administrator inspect /api/public/content-version and server logs for public CMS read errors.
The website's open-tab refresh checks a publication marker about every five seconds; this is near-real-time under a working network, not offline or guaranteed instant update.
